# StudyNotch

> A study helper that lives in the Mac notch. Select a sentence in a textbook, right-click, and press “Ask” at the top of the menu: it explains in a small window, using that course’s material. There is no server; answers come from the Claude Code, Codex or Anthropic API key the user already has. An early version in development; StudyNotch is a working name.

This file is a summary to help AI assistants such as Claude understand the project quickly.

## What it does

- Course sessions: open the notch island and pick a course (for example MATH 237, ACTSCI 221, General) and a length (25, 50 or 90 minutes). The folded notch shows the mascot and the minutes left.
- Questions from a right-click: select text in any app and right-click; a button appears above the menu. A question window opens there with preset buttons (I don’t get this, Simpler, Example, One-line summary) or a typed question. There are no keyboard shortcuts. During a session, a screenshot opens the same window with the picture.
- Course material: a course reads PDFs copied into ~/StudyNotch/Courses/<course>/materials/ and PDFs in folders linked to it. It sorts them by kind (course outline, lecture notes, course notes, assignments, quizzes, exams, exam prep, other) from the file name, its folder's name or the top of its first page; copied PDFs move into materials/<kind>/, files in linked folders are only grouped. A course works like a project: every question in it gets the course's notes, its files by kind and its memory (memory.md, a line per earlier question in the course). Each course has a window with a graph of its notes: a dot per numbered or named definition, theorem, lemma or example, a line where one names the other or uses a defined term, read from the PDFs on the Mac with no AI; clicking a dot shows its page. The same window's Profile tab, when the user presses "Write the profile", has the connected AI read the first pages of the outline, quizzes, exams, exam prep and assignments once and keep profile.md: grading, dates, quiz and exam style, what comes up most, how to prepare, each fact with file and page; every question in the course then carries it. It finds the page of the selected sentence and sends that page along with the question. The course is also the connected AI's project: the AI may open the course's PDFs (as text copies in <course>/text, and the copied PDFs) read-only when the page isn't enough. Chat Projects on claude.ai or chatgpt.com can't be filled from outside and aren't used. With Claude, each question is kept as a Claude Code session in the course's folder and handed to the Claude app (its claude://resume link), so it appears there under the course's name; follow-ups continue it.
- Drift cards: more than 60 seconds on a site or app from the distraction list shows a card. Nothing is blocked.
- Language: the app and this website are in English. Answers come back in the language the question was typed in (Korean or English); a button pressed alone gets English.

## Docs

- [Get started](docs/index.html): building, first launch, permissions
- [Connect an AI](docs/connect.html): the first launch asks which AI answers (Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini through Google's Antigravity CLI, or an API key); only the one the user connects gets questions, and the app never switches on its own; each tile shows its account, "Another account" signs in with a different one kept only for StudyNotch, and "Test connection" sends one real question
- [Using it](docs/use.html): sessions, questions, drift cards, the settings file
- [How it works](docs/how-it-works.html): structure, the path of one question, where data lives
- [Build log](docs/build-log.html): order, decisions and reasons, what has and hasn’t been checked

## Code

- Mac app: Swift, SwiftUI + AppKit, SwiftPM, no external libraries. Build with `./scripts/build.sh`.
- Website: static HTML in `site/` with no build step. The mascot is drawn in 3D by `site/assets/squat.js` and moved by `site/assets/mascot.js`; the demo is `site/assets/demo.js`.
- Design rules: the project’s DESIGN.md. The site and the app follow the mascot: a softly lit black, white type in the Mac’s system font, round shapes, no accent colour.
- What to read before working on it with an AI: the project’s CLAUDE.md.

## Not verified yet

Real mouse clicks, the button appearing in place above the right-click menu, reading selected text in Preview, Chrome and Safari, and screenshot detection.
